nameStory: Whorled pennywort gets its 'pennywort' name from its perfectly round, coin-shaped leaves that look like tiny green pennies scattered across wet ground. The 'whorled' part comes from how its small flowers are arranged in circular clusters, or whorls, around the stem like tiny umbrellas.
description: Whorled pennywort is a low-growing, creeping plant that spreads along the ground in wet areas like a living green carpet. Its most distinctive feature is its perfectly round, shield-shaped leaves that sit on long, thin stalks rising from creeping stems. The plant stays close to the ground, rarely getting taller than a few inches, but can spread widely through marshy areas with its trailing, rooting stems.

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Perfectly circular, coin-sized leaves that feel smooth and slightly waxy to the touch, attached to the center of the leaf rather than at the edge like a tiny green umbrella

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Creeping, mat-forming stems that root at joints and spread along muddy or wet surfaces, creating patches of round leaves

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Tiny, inconspicuous whitish flowers arranged in small circular clusters (whorls) on short stalks, easy to miss among the distinctive leaves

idTips.label: Leaf Stalks
idTips.description: Long, thin, smooth leaf stems that emerge from creeping runners and hold each round leaf upright like a tiny parasol

habitat: Look for whorled pennywort in consistently moist to wet areas like marsh edges, pond shores, muddy streambanks, and boggy spots. It thrives in areas that stay soggy year-round and can even grow partially submerged in shallow water.

seasonality.spring: New round leaves emerge on fresh shoots as the plant begins its growing season, creating expanding mats of perfectly circular foliage.
seasonality.summer: Peak growing season with full leaf development and tiny flower clusters appearing, though the distinctive round leaves remain the main identifying feature.
seasonality.fall: Leaves may yellow and die back in colder areas, though in milder spots the plant can remain somewhat evergreen through autumn.
seasonality.winter: In New England, the above-ground parts typically die back, but the creeping root system survives to regrow in spring.

funFact: This little plant is so adaptable to aquatic life that aquarium enthusiasts around the world grow it as an underwater carpet plant, where it can live completely submerged and still photosynthesize through its round, shield-like leaves!
confusionNotes: The perfectly round, centrally-attached leaves make whorled pennywort nearly impossible to confuse with anything else - most plants have leaves attached at the edge or base, not dead center like a tiny green umbrella.
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called 'pennywort,' this plant is actually in the ivy family (Araliaceae), making it a distant relative of English ivy and ginseng rather than the true pennyworts, showing how common names can sometimes mislead us about plant relationships.
compareHints: Among New England's pennyworts, whorled pennywort is the easiest to identify because of its perfectly circular leaves attached at the center. American water-pennywort has kidney-shaped leaves with a notch, while floating marsh pennywort has leaves that are more deeply lobed and divided, lacking that perfect coin-like appearance.

relatedSpecies.distinction: American water-pennywort can be distinguished from its relatives by its consistently round leaves and preference for the northeastern climate.
Among New England's water pennyworts, manyflower marshpennywort has the most perfectly circular leaves and the most obvious umbrella-shaped flower clusters.
Unlike American Water-pennywort which has kidney-shaped or lobed leaves, Sibthorp's Pennywort has perfectly round, unlobed leaves.
Unlike its pennywort relatives in New England, floating marsh pennywort is the only one that forms true floating mats on open water.
**[UNCERTAIN]** Compared to its more common cousin American Water-pennywort, this species likely differs in leaf size, flower arrangement, or specific habitat requirements.
